descriptor: Retirement Villages / Aged Care · reported in NZD

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Summerset Group Holdings Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Summerset Group Holdings Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

development.title: Development
development.content:
Units delivered and the development margin earned on them.

For Summerset Group Holdings Limited: development margin is cash realised on first sale; a fall signals build-cost or pricing pressure.

What to watch:

  • Units delivered against the pipeline
  • Development margin trend

dmf.title: Deferred management fees & care revenue
dmf.content:
DMF accrues over a resident's tenure and is realised on resale. Care fees & village services is the recurring revenue earned from operating care beds and village services.

For Summerset Group Holdings Limited: together these are the two cash revenue streams that recur regardless of the housing market; reported net income is dominated by unrealised revaluations instead.

What to watch:

  • DMF growth against units in portfolio
  • Care revenue growth against care beds operated

nta.title: Net tangible assets per share
nta.content:
NTA per share is shareholders' equity per share, Summerset's own disclosed metric and the asset-value anchor management reports against.

For Summerset Group Holdings Limited: grows mainly from property revaluations and retained underlying profit, so it is the balance-sheet counterpart to the underlying-profit income statement.

What to watch:

  • NTA growth against the share price (premium/discount)
  • Whether growth is revaluation-driven or earnings-driven

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
Basic EPS is reported net income per share (revaluation gains included); DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Summerset Group Holdings Limited: EPS here swings with property revaluations, so the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) is noisier than DPS against underlying profit per share.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from underlying profit, not revaluation gains

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Summerset Group Holdings Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Summerset Group Holdings Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

oraSales.title: ORA sales
oraSales.content:
Sales of occupation right agreements: new sales from developments, resales of existing units, and the total of the two.

For Summerset Group Holdings Limited: resale volumes drive deferred management fee realisation; new sales fund development. Total volume is the throughput the DMF and development-margin lines are earned on.

What to watch:

  • Resale volumes against stock available
  • Pricing versus the housing market

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Summerset Group Holdings Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Summerset Group Holdings Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Summerset Group Holdings Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

underlying.title: Underlying profit
underlying.content:
Underlying profit removes unrealised revaluation gains from reported net income.

For Summerset Group Holdings Limited: the valuation capitalises underlying profit; reported NPAT is not comparable year to year.

What to watch:

  • Underlying profit growth
  • Share of profit from resales versus new sales

units.title: Units in portfolio
units.content:
Retirement units and care beds operated.

For Summerset Group Holdings Limited: the installed base that DMF and care fees are earned on.

What to watch:

  • Growth from development versus acquisition

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
